scope: Offline fixed-background pixel consistency; not calibrated visual odometry or physical success
finding: All57 saved camera frames retain four fixed-background template matches at the same integer pixel locations; over54 overlapping frames mapped sensor heading changes -65.5964degrees. This strengthens prior evidence of a sensor-heading/scene-motion discrepancy without calibrating camera angles or identifying the underlying cause.

sensor_comparison.selection: Last sensor host receipt at or before camera host receipt, restricted to recorded sensor span and at most50ms prior; not exposure synchronization

independent_review: All57 input hashes and pairings verified;696 direct/FFT spot comparisons across first/middle/last images; peer receipt included.
limitations: Only saved snapshots, not all received frames; motion between saved exposures is unknown
Matching is integer-pixel resolution; zero offset does not imply zero subpixel motion. Raw fisheye pixels are not world angle, distance or camera pose
Host timestamps do not guarantee synchronized camera exposure/IMU sample time
Fixed-background templates were selected manually; this study is not a general motion validator
Large field-of-view changes/occlusion can break local template search; preserve correlation scores and search-boundary flags
excluded_approach: Unbounded nearest-prior sensor pairing would reuse stale final readings for the last3 camera frames; these are explicitly excluded from the matched heading calculation.
